citation: Tikhonov AP, SanMiguel PJ, Nakajima Y, Gorenstein NM, Bennetzen JL, Avramova Z (1999) Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 96(13):7409-7414 (deposit, nesting structure); Meyers BC, Tingey SV, Morgante M (2001) Genome Res 11(10):1660-1676, Table 1 (independent Ty1-copia classification of the Victim family)

citation: Tikhonov AP, SanMiguel PJ, Nakajima Y, Gorenstein NM, Bennetzen JL, Avramova Z (1999) Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 96(13):7409-7414 (deposit, nesting structure); Meyers BC, Tingey SV, Morgante M (2001) Genome Res 11(10):1660-1676, Table 1 (independent Ty3-gypsy classification of the Milt family)

citation: Turner G, Barbulescu M, Su M, Jensen-Seaman MI, Kidd KK & Lenz J 2001 Current Biology 11:1531
why_safe: Turner et al. sequenced both LTRs of this human-specific, insertionally polymorphic provirus and found 'no sequence differences between the 5' and 3' LTR' -- i.e., 100% LTR-LTR identity -- giving an estimated insertion time of 100,000-200,000 years. HML-2/LTR5Hs family membership is established by prior phylogenetic classification (Mayer/Coffin lineage work) independent of any TE-annotation tool. Youngest anchor of the >=98% bucket, cross-kingdom counterpart to the fly data.

citation: Subramanian RP, Wildschutte JH, Russo C & Coffin JM 2011 Retrovirology 8:90
why_safe: Subramanian et al. report an estimated age of 1.61-2.91 My for this human-specific, polymorphic HML-2 locus, calculated from LTR-LTR substitution frequency divided by their stated clock (0.24%/My upper bound, 0.45%/My lower bound). Back-solving that formula gives an implied LTR-LTR identity of roughly 99.3% (substitution ~0.7%) -- a value I derived from their stated rate and age range, not a percentage printed directly in the paper, hence medium rather than high confidence on the exact number (the accession and HML-2 family call are high confidence).

citation: Subramanian RP, Wildschutte JH, Russo C & Coffin JM 2011 Retrovirology 8:90
why_safe: Human-specific HML-2 locus, reported age 6.32-11.44 My. Applying the paper's stated substitution-rate formula gives an implied LTR-LTR identity of ~97.2% (derived, not printed directly). Falls at the top of the 85-97% intermediate band.

citation: Karn J, Brenner S, Barnett L (1983) Protein structural domains in the Caenorhabditis elegans unc-54 myosin heavy chain gene are not separated by introns. Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 80(14):4253-4257

expected_class: not a TE - host protein-coding gene (vegetative actin, ACT2), single-copy genomic clone with 2 introns

expected_class: not a TE - host protein-coding gene (actin, ACT1), single-copy essential gene with one intron
citation: NCBI Gene ID 850504 (ACT1/YFL039C), cross-referenced to Saccharomyces Genome Database locus S000001855, chromosome VI reference sequence NC_001138.5
why_safe: ACT1 is single-copy and essential; its one intron is only ~308 bp, far too short to contain a Ty retrotransposon (~5.9 kb) or even a full solo LTR. Ty elements in S. cerevisiae preferentially target Pol III-transcribed (tRNA-gene-flanking) regions, not ACT1.

expected_class: not a TE - host protein-coding gene (beta-globin, HBB), single-copy gene with 2 introns

expected_class: not a TE - centromeric alpha-satellite tandem repeat (171-bp AT-rich consensus monomer); satellite DNA, not a mobile element

expected_class: not a TE - simple/low-complexity CGG trinucleotide microsatellite in the FMR1 5' UTR

citation: Fu YH, Kuhl DP, Pizzuti A, et al. (1991) Variation of the CGG repeat at the fragile X site results in genetic instability: resolution of the Sherman paradox. Cell 67(6):1047-1058
why_safe: Pure trinucleotide microsatellite with no coding capacity. Its GC-richness and copy-number polymorphism can trigger low-complexity/simple-repeat masking, but it has no similarity to any TE domain or terminal-repeat structure.

expected_class: not a TE - host telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT/hEST2), single-copy nuclear gene, mRNA/complete cds
citation: Meyerson M, Counter CM, Eaton EN, et al. (1997) hEST2, the putative human telomerase catalytic subunit gene, is up-regulated in tumor cells and during immortalization. Cell 90(4):785-795
why_safe: TERT carries a bona fide reverse-transcriptase fold and is a top false-positive risk for RT-domain-based TE detectors; it is single-copy, nuclear-encoded, essential for telomere maintenance, and its RT activity was directly assayed biochemically on the telomerase RNA template, independent of any TE annotation.

expected_class: reverse-transcriptase domain of a self-splicing group II intron (Ll.LtrB, protein LtrA) - falls outside the Wicker eukaryotic TE classification scheme rather than being a TE proper
citation: Mills DA, McKay LL, Dunny GM (1996) Splicing of a group II intron involved in the conjugative transfer of pRS01 in lactococci. J Bacteriol 178(12):3531-3538
why_safe: LtrA has an authentic RT domain, evolutionarily ancestral to non-LTR retrotransposon and telomerase RTs, and is a frequent close bacterial hit for RT-domain searches. Ll.LtrB is nonetheless a catalytic-RNA self-splicing intron with an intron-encoded protein (retrohoming mechanism) rather than a Wicker-scheme transposable element; its single-copy context interrupting the conjugative relaxase gene ltrB was established experimentally, independent of any TE caller. Labeled with a softened class string rather than a flat 'not a TE' because group II introns are themselves mobile genetic elements under some classification schemes.

expected_class: not a TE - host AP endonuclease (APEX1/APE1/HAP1), single-copy base-excision-repair enzyme
citation: Robson CN, Hickson ID (1991) Isolation of cDNA clones encoding a human apurinic/apyrimidinic endonuclease that corrects DNA repair and mutagenesis defects in E. coli xth (exonuclease III) mutants. Nucleic Acids Res 19(20):5519-5523

It is single-copy, essential, nuclear-encoded, carries no RT or transposase domain, and its AP-endonuclease activity was defined biochemically independent of any TE annotation.

expected_class: not a TE - host chromosomal tyrosine recombinase (XerC), single-copy site-specific recombinase for chromosome-dimer resolution
citation: Colloms SD, Sykora P, Szatmari G, Sherratt DJ (1990) Recombination at ColE1 cer requires the Escherichia coli xerC gene product, a member of the lambda integrase family of site-specific recombinases. J Bacteriol 172(12):6973-6980
why_safe: XerC is a catalytic-tyrosine site-specific recombinase of the lambda-integrase family. This tyrosine-recombinase fold, rather than the DDE-transposase fold used by most DNA transposons, is what Crypton DNA transposons and DIRS-like retroelements use for integration, making it a genuine confusion axis for domain panels. XerC's role in dif-site recombination for chromosome dimer resolution was established biochemically and genetically, independent of any TE database.

expected_class: not a TE - host spliceosomal protein (PRP8/YHR165C) whose core domain is a degenerate, catalytically repurposed reverse transcriptase/maturase/endonuclease/RNase-H-like fold retained from an ancestral retroelement

why_safe: PRP8's central conserved domain is structurally homologous to group-II-intron-maturase/retroelement RT-fingers-palm, thumb/X, and endonuclease-like subdomains - almost the full TE RT+EN domain architecture - yet it is single-copy, essential, and functions as the catalytic scaffold of the spliceosome, not as a mobile element; its RT-like fold is catalytically dead/repurposed, established by structural and phylogenetic analysis independent of any TE caller.

citation: Leblanc P, Desset S, Dastugue B, Vaury C. 1997. EMBO J 16(24):7521-7531
why_safe: ZAM, shown experimentally to have all structural (gag-pol-env) and functional features of a retrovirus and grouped with the canonical gypsy clade (gypsy, 297, 17.6, ZAM); complete 8435 bp gag/pol/env record.

citation: Desset S, Conte C, Dimitri P, Calco V, Dastugue B, Vaury C. 1999. Mol Biol Evol 16(1):54-66
why_safe: Idefix, characterized alongside ZAM as a mobilized gypsy-clade retroelement regulated by the flamenco locus. Record is explicitly labeled 'partial' (gag/pol/env genes, partial), 7411 bp -- useful for domain content but not guaranteed full-length boundaries.

citation: Molto MD, Paricio N, Lopez-Preciado MA, Semeshin VF, Martinez-Sebastian MJ. 1996. J Mol Evol 42:369-375
why_safe: Tirant, described as gag-pol-env organized and strongly similar to ZAM, part of the gypsy-clade tirant/zam/idefix/17.6/297 group; record is 5184 bp, shorter than the ~8527 bp full-length element reported in later work, so likely represents a partial/defective genomic copy rather than the complete consensus.

citation: Sanz-Alferez S, SanMiguel P, Jin YK, Springer PS, Bennetzen JL. 2003. Genome 46(5):745-752
why_safe: Cinful-1, an 8581 bp complete-sequence record, explicitly classified as Ty3-gypsy type. Caveat: the paper reports Cinful-1/2 lack gag homology (a defective element for gag content), so this record is best used for pol/LTR structure rather than full gag-pol-env domain testing.

citation: SanMiguel P, Bennetzen JL. 1998. Ann Bot 82(Suppl A):37-44
why_safe: Tekay, explicitly titled in GenBank as a 'gypsy/Ty3-type retrotransposon,' complete 12118 bp sequence.

citation: Avramova Z, Tikhonov A, SanMiguel P, Jin YK, Liu C, Woo SS, Wing RA, Bennetzen JL. 1996. Plant J 10(6):1163-1168
why_safe: Reina, explicitly deposited as a 'Gypsy-like retrotransposon'; 5412 bp record from the paper that first named and localized this low-copy maize element.

citation: Butler M, Goodwin T, Poulter R. 2001. Mol Biol Evol 18(3):443-447
why_safe: Gmr1, a full-length (5269 bp) vertebrate LTR retrotransposon placed in the Ty3/gypsy group by sequence-similarity phylogeny, with LTRs stated to be 98% identical. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: Gmr1 has an unusual pol domain order (protease-integrase-RT/RNase H) matching the Ty1/copia arrangement rather than the canonical Ty3/gypsy protease-RT/RNase H-integrase order -- this is a documented exception explicitly discussed by the authors, not a labeling error, and should be treated as a deliberately atypical stress-test case rather than a canonical Gypsy exemplar if domain order is part of the classifier's decision logic.

citation: Rocheta M, Cordeiro J, Marum L, Farinha N, Amaral P, Sobral R, Miguel C. 2012. BMC Res Notes 5:432
why_safe: Corky, explicitly deposited as a gypsy-like retrotransposon, complete 5924 bp sequence, homologous to other characterized Pinaceae gypsy elements (IFG7, PpRT1).

citation: McHale MT, Roberts IN, Noble SA, Beaumont C, Whitehead MP, Seth D, Oliver RP. 1992. Mol Gen Genet 233(3):337-347
why_safe: CfT-1, complete 7397 bp sequence; paper states LTRs of 427 bp and a pol ORF with domain order protease-RT-RNaseH-integrase, closely related to the gypsy class of LTR retrotransposons. Current species name is Fulvia fulva (synonym of Cladosporium fulvum).

citation: Dobinson KF, Harris RE, Hamer JE. 1993. Mol Plant Microbe Interact 6:114-126
why_safe: Grasshopper (grh), complete gag/pol cds (5233 bp); paper states 198 bp LTRs and a pol ORF (RT-RNaseH-integrase order) related to the gypsy family.

citation: Kobayashi S, Goto-Yamamoto N, Hirochika H. 2004. Science 304(5673):982
why_safe: Gret1, explicitly deposited/titled as a 'gypsy-type retrotransposon'; its insertion into the VvMybA1 promoter was experimentally linked to loss of grape skin pigmentation, an independent functional confirmation of the element's identity and locus.

citation: Anaya N, Roncero MI. 1995. Mol Gen Genet 249(6):637-647
why_safe: Skippy, complete gag/pol cds (8457 bp); paper states 429 bp LTRs and a pol domain order (protease-RT-RNaseH-integrase) closely related to the gypsy family.

citation: Kossack DS, Kinlaw CS. 1999. Plant Mol Biol 39(3):417-426
why_safe: IFG7, deposited as 'gypsy-like retroposon...complete genome' (5937 bp); paper title states it 'has an extensive history in pines' and confirms gypsy-like sequence features.

citation: Rocheta M, Cordeiro J, Oliveira M, Miguel C. 2007. Planta 225(3):551-562
why_safe: PpRT1, the paper's title states it is 'the first complete gypsy-like retrotransposon isolated in Pinus pinaster'; complete-sequence record, 5966 bp, matching the paper's stated length.

citation: Salina EA, Sergeeva EM, Adonina IG, Shcherban AB, Belcram H, Huneau C, Chalhoub B. 2011. BMC Plant Biol 11:99
why_safe: One of three Fatima (Ty3-gypsy) elements explicitly annotated with coordinates in this BAC sequence; both flanking LTRs are 473 bp (5' 102728-103200, 3' 112206-112678), an unusually clean matched-LTR pair useful for panel 5.2 boundary comparison. Flanked by an ACATC target-site duplication per the annotation.

citation: Tikhonov AP, SanMiguel PJ, Nakajima Y, Gorenstein NM, Bennetzen JL, Avramova Z. 1999. Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 96(13):7409-7414
why_safe: A non-truncated Huck-family (Ty3/gypsy) copy with explicit element coordinates annotated in the finished maize adh1 region; Huck superfamily assignment independently established in the maize LTR-retrotransposon literature (SanMiguel/Bennetzen lineage of papers).

citation: Kimberland ML, Divoky V, Prchal J, Schwahn U, Berger W, Kazazian HH Jr. 1999. Hum Mol Genet 8(8):1557-1560
why_safe: L1RP, a full-length, retrotransposition-competent ('hot') human L1 in intron 1 of the RP2 gene. GenBank record (6019 bp) annotates intact ORF1 (338 codons) and ORF2 (1275 codons; nt 1987-5814). L1 elements canonically terminate in a poly-A tail required for target-primed reverse transcription (Feng et al. 1996 Cell 87:905-916); this is clade-level structural knowledge, not a base-by-base re-verification of this specific record's terminal poly-A tract in this session.

citation: Naas TP, DeBerardinis RJ, Moran JV, Ostertag EM, Kingsmore SF, Seldin MF, Hayashizaki Y, Martin SL, Kazazian HH Jr. 1998. EMBO J 17(2):590-597
why_safe: L1spa (TF subfamily), a full-length, retrotransposition-competent mouse L1 that inserted de novo into the Glrb gene causing the spastic mouse phenotype (Kingsmore et al. 1994 Nat Genet 7:136-141). GenBank record (9278 bp) annotates ORF1 (nt 3142-4257) and ORF2 (nt 4298-8143). Naas et al. 1998 explicitly state a 667 bp 3' UTR 'terminating in a stretch of adenines' — poly-A tail directly confirmed in the primary paper, not inferred.

citation: Fawcett DH, Lister CK, Kellett E, Finnegan DJ. 1986. Cell 47(6):1007-1015
why_safe: Full-length I-factor clone (6231 bp) with annotated ORF1 (nt 286-1566) and ORF2 (nt 1635-5294). Importantly, I elements do NOT terminate in a poly-A tail: primary literature (Chambeyron et al. 2002 Nucleic Acids Res 30:3387-3395) established that I-clade elements end instead in 3-8 tandem TAA/UAA repeats. Full-length, non-poly-A-tailed structural contrast case.

citation: Priimagi AF, Mizrokhi LJ, Ilyin YV. 1988. Gene 70(2):253-262
why_safe: Near full-length Jockey clone 'J-1' (5154 bp; ORF1 <414-2165, 5' end of ORF1 slightly beyond the clone's UTR margin; ORF2 2162-4912). Priimagi et al. 1988 explicitly state a complete jockey copy 'is terminated with an oligodeoxynucleotide (dA) sequence' -- i.e. a poly(dA)/poly-A-like 3' tail, consistent with the terminal A-rich stretch of this record. Positive control for a poly-A-tailed LINE outside the L1/L1-related clades.

citation: Fujimoto H, et al. 2004. Nucleic Acids Res 32(4):1555-1565; clade originally described by Burke WD, Müller F, Eickbush TH. 1987. Mol Cell Biol 7(6):2221-2230
why_safe: R2Bm element (~4.2 kb) inserted into the 28S rRNA gene; single ORF (nt 658-4002) fusing reverse transcriptase and restriction-enzyme-like endonuclease domains -- the diagnostic R2-clade architecture (no separate ORF1/gag-like domain). R2 elements are established in the primary literature (Burke et al. 1987; Eickbush 2002 in Mobile DNA II) to lack a poly-A tail, instead ending in a structured, self-priming 3' UTR; the terminal ~80 nt of this record are GC-rich/structured rather than a homopolymeric A-tract, consistent with that.

citation: Jakubczak JL, Xiong Y, Eickbush TH. 1990. J Mol Biol 212(1):37-52
why_safe: Full-length-scale R1Dm clone (5356 bp) with two ORFs: ORF I (nt 319-1734, protease-like) and ORF II (nt 1728-4793, reverse transcriptase/integrase) -- the R1(LOA)-clade domain architecture, sister clade to R2. Superfamily left blank because R1-clade Wicker-superfamily naming is not fully standardized; clade identity (R1) is unambiguous. Like R2, R1 elements lack a canonical poly-A tail; the 3' terminus here is AT-rich rather than a homopolymeric A stretch.

citation: Burke WD, Müller F, Eickbush TH. 1995. Nucleic Acids Res 23(22):4628-4634
why_safe: Full-length R4 element (4686 bp) inserted into the 26S (large-subunit) rRNA gene. R4 is an ancient non-LTR clade encoding only a single ORF (restriction-enzyme-like endonuclease domain, no separate ORF1/gag-like domain) -- structurally distinct from L1/I/Jockey/R1/R2. Superfamily left blank (R4 clade, not a standard Wicker superfamily label) but the clade assignment itself is not in doubt. Useful single-ORF, non-poly-A contrast case.

citation: Youngman S, van Luenen HGAM, Plasterk RHA. 1996. FEBS Lett 380(1-2):1-7
why_safe: Complete RTE-1 element (3291 bp) with a single ORF (~625 aa, RT-similar) -- the RTE-clade single-ORF architecture (RTE established as a distinct, widely distributed clade by Malik & Eickbush 1998 Mol Biol Evol 15:1123-1134). Full-length, structurally simple non-LTR retrotransposon distinct from all L1/I/Jockey/R1/R2/R4 cases above.

citation: Zatsepina OG, Velikodvorskaia VV, Molodtsov VB, Garbuz D, Lerman DN, Bettencourt BR, Feder ME, Evgen'ev MB. 2001. J Exp Biol 204(Pt 11):1869-1881
why_safe: 5'-TRUNCATED case. GenBank explicitly annotates a 'truncated Jockey element transposon' at nt 360-1806 (1446 bp) adjacent to the Hsp70Ba gene -- roughly 29% of the ~5020 bp full-length Jockey (compare M22874 above), i.e. missing the 5' end and retaining only part of the element. Direct positive example of the common truncated genomic state for this clade; poly-A/3' status not separately assessed since the truncation removed the diagnostic 5' region, not the 3' end.

citation: Woods-Samuels P, Wong C, Mathias SL, Scott AF, Kazazian HH Jr, Antonarakis SE. 1989. Genomics 4(3):290-296
why_safe: 5'-TRUNCATED case (clone JH27L1HS, 3785 bp). Woods-Samuels et al. 1989 characterize this as a nondeleterious L1 insertion in an intron of the human factor VIII gene retaining an ORF spanning most of the clone (nt 1-3580), corresponding to the 3' portion of L1 ORF2 -- i.e. 5' end missing, 3' portion retained. Truncation and clade identity are established directly in the primary paper; the terminal poly-A tract specifically was not independently re-verified from the raw sequence in this session (automated position extraction proved unreliable), so treat the poly-A detail, not the truncation/identity call, as unconfirmed.

citation: Woods-Samuels P, Wong C, Mathias SL, Scott AF, Kazazian HH Jr, Antonarakis SE. 1989. Genomics 4(3):290-296
why_safe: 5'-TRUNCATED case (clone JH28L1HS, 2132 bp), a second, independent nondeleterious L1 insertion in the same factor VIII intron reported in the same paper, with an ORF at nt 1-1927. Same caveat as M22333: truncation/identity solid from the primary paper; terminal poly-A specifically not independently re-verified this session.

citation: Sekido R, Takagi T, Okanami M, Moribe H, Yamamura M, Higashi Y, Kondoh H. 1996. Gene 173(2):227-232
why_safe: 5'-TRUNCATED CR1 case. GenBank feature table explicitly annotates a mobile_element of type 'transposon:CR1' at nt 417-952 (536 bp) within an intron of the chicken deltaEF1 gene locus. Full-length CR1 is ~4.5 kb (Haas et al. 1997 J Mol Evol); a 536 bp fragment is therefore heavily 5'-truncated, consistent with Vandergon & Reitman's (1994 Mol Biol Evol 11:886-898) finding that the vast majority of genomic CR1 copies are heavily 5'-truncated. No ORF or poly-A is annotated at this locus; CR1, like other R1-like clade members, is not expected to carry a poly-A tail.

citation: Storer J, Hubley R, Rosen J, Wheeler TJ, Smit AFA. 2021. Mobile DNA 12:2 (Dfam resource); clade established by Kordiš D, Gubenšek F. 1998. Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 95(18):10704-10709
why_safe: Dfam-curated family DF000002968 (BovB-1_DR), classified LINE > RTE-group > BovB in zebrafish. BovB is the classic horizontally-transferred RTE-clade LINE (Kordiš & Gubenšek 1998); Dfam family-membership is curated independently of any TEagle-adjacent tool. This is a consensus family model, not a single genomic locus with coordinates, and no poly-A status is assessable at this level -- flagged as lower-resolution evidence than the discrete-locus cases above.

citation: Storer J, Hubley R, Rosen J, Wheeler TJ, Smit AFA. 2021. Mobile DNA 12:2 (Dfam resource); Batzer MA, Deininger PL. 2002. Nat Rev Genet 3(5):370-379
why_safe: Dfam family DF000000002 = AluY, the youngest/most active human Alu subfamily, curated independently of any TEagle output. NON-AUTONOMOUS: Alu elements have no ORFs or reverse transcriptase of their own and are mobilized in trans by L1 ORF2p (Dewannieux et al. 2003 Nat Genet 35:41-48). TEagle is not expected to classify this as an autonomous LINE; correctly declining an autonomous-LINE call here is itself informative.

citation: Storer J, Hubley R, Rosen J, Wheeler TJ, Smit AFA. 2021. Mobile DNA 12:2 (Dfam resource); Krayev AS, Kramerov DA, Skryabin KG, Ryskov AP, Bayev AA, Georgiev GP. 1980. Nucleic Acids Res 8(6):1201-1215
why_safe: Dfam family DF000001733 = B1_Mm, the mouse counterpart of primate Alu (both derived from 7SL RNA, independently amplified). NON-AUTONOMOUS SINE: no ORF1/ORF2 of its own, mobilized in trans by an autonomous LINE partner.

citation: Medhora, Maruyama & Hartl 1991 Genetics 128(2):311-318
why_safe: Identity high (record clone=Mos1, matches the canonical Medhora/Maruyama/Hartl 1991 Mos1 papers) but the GenBank record is PARTIAL at both ends (misc_feature <1..>1293) with NO annotated CDS or TIR coordinates. Do not claim record-level TIR/ORF coordinates - cite the paper's reported 28-bp TIRs instead. Autonomous per literature.

citation: Franz & Savakis 1991 Nucleic Acids Res 19(23):6646
why_safe: TIR coordinates (1-255 inverted / 1521-1775 inverted) and Tc1-like family identity are solid GenBank-annotated features. Do NOT use as an 'autonomous, TIR-encloses-intact-transposase' example: the deposited copy's transposase region includes a /pseudo-annotated segment (gene/CDS 887..1492, note=pseudo) alongside CDS 347..808 - this specific clone is not confirmed fully functional.

citation: Hehl, Nacken, Krause, Saedler & Sommer 1991 Plant Mol Biol 16(2):369-371
why_safe: GenBank-annotated 12-bp TIRs (repeat_region 1-12 and 3617-3629, both inverted) directly enclose the Tam3-transposase CDS (848-3097, protein_id CAA38906.1). Autonomous, full-length, coordinates explicit.

citation: Streck, MacGaffey & Beckendorf 1986 EMBO J 5(13):3615-3623
why_safe: GenBank-annotated left/right terminal repeats (1-12 / 2999-3016) enclose ORF1/transposase CDS (316-2250, protein_id CAA28410.1). This is the classic hobo108 element; explicit coordinates.

citation: Warren, Atkinson & O'Brochta 1994 Genet Res 64(2):87-97
why_safe: GenBank-annotated inverted TIRs (1-17 / 2733-2749) enclose the complete transposase CDS (450-2288). Autonomous, explicit coordinates.

citation: Nacken, Piotrowiak, Saedler & Sommer 1991 Mol Gen Genet 228(1-2):201-208
why_safe: 13-bp inverted TIRs (1-13 / 15152-15164) explicitly enclose both TNP1 (multi-exon CDS) and TNP2 CDS regions of the Tam1 element in the GenBank feature table. Structural homology to maize En/Spm reported in the paper. Autonomous.

citation: Zabala & Vodkin 2008 BMC Plant Biol 8:124
why_safe: 'Putative autonomous' per the paper's own title. GenBank mobile_element feature gives explicit subrange coordinates (4240-24783, ~20.5 kb) for the Tgmt* CACTA element within a larger F3'H-flanking genomic deposit. Paper text (not broken out as separate GenBank sub-features) reports 13-bp CACTA-type TIRs and a 2194-aa TNP1/TNP2-domain transposase spanning most of the element.

citation: Xu, Yan, Maurais, Fu, O'Brien, Mottinger & Dooner 2004 Plant Cell 16(5):1105-1114
why_safe: GenBank-annotated 185-bp inverted TIRs (1-185 / 3736-3916) enclose the transposase CDS (join 746-2484,2554-2944, protein_id AAF66982.1). Flag as an atypical/distant Mutator relative: paper reports Jittery excises without reinsertion and its transposase (JITA) is closer to MULE-family MURA proteins than to canonical MuDR.

citation: Li, Harris & Dooner 2013 Plant Cell 25(9):3251-3265
why_safe: GenBank record itself annotates the mobile_element as note='autonomous TED element'; a multi-exon transposase CDS ('TEDA', 513 aa, protein_id AGR45850.1) spans the element. Companion locus record KF279654 shows 9-bp flanking TSDs (1505-1513/5474-5482) bracketing the same 3960-bp element in a bronze1 (bz-m175) insertion. TIR base-pair count is described in the paper rather than itemized as a separate GenBank repeat_region feature in either record.

citation: Cary, Goebel, Corsaro, Wang, Rosen & Fraser 1989 Virology 172(1):156-169
why_safe: GenBank-annotated terminal (1-13/2460-2472) and internal (17-36/2410-2428) inverted repeats enclose the transposase CDS (329-2113, protein_id AAA87375.2). This is the original piggyBac/IFP2 clone, independent of TEagle's excluded M11240 (verified separately to actually be a D. melanogaster copia LTR retrotransposon record, not piggyBac).

citation: Luo, Li, Han, Guo, Yang, Wu, Zhang, Liu, Qian & Fang 2014 BMC Mol Biol 15:28
why_safe: GenBank-annotated outer (1-13/2394-2406) and inner (352-376/2247-2271) inverted repeats enclose the transposase CDS (613-2130, protein_id AGK25052.1). Independent second piggyBac-like case, different organism from IFP2 and from TEagle's own OQ718454 (excluded for other reasons, see supply_assessment).

coords: 996..3902 (mobile_element span within a 4734-bp deposited plasmid record)
citation: O'Hare & Rubin 1983 Cell 34(1):25-35
why_safe: CAVEAT FIRST: the deposited GenBank record's own SOURCE field is 'synthetic construct' - this is a cloned transformation-vector plasmid (pPI25.1), not a genomic insertion. That said, the annotated mobile_element span (996-3902) is exactly 2907 bp, matching the well-documented complete P-element length, flanked by GenBank-annotated 8-bp direct repeats (988-995/3903-3910) consistent with target-site duplication footprint reported by O'Hare & Rubin 1983. Confidence held at medium specifically because of the vector-context caveat.

citation: Black, Jackson, Kidwell & Dover 1987 EMBO J 6(13):4125-4135
why_safe: NON-AUTONOMOUS: internally-deleted P-element derivative (1170 bp vs the 2907-bp complete P element). TIRs preserved and GenBank-annotated (inverted repeat A: 9-39, inverted repeat A': 1132-1162) but NO transposase CDS is annotated - the transposase-encoding region is deleted; the element instead encodes the truncated KP repressor protein. TEagle should not call this autonomous.

citation: Kikuchi, Terauchi, Wada & Hirano 2003 Nature 421(6919):167-170
why_safe: NON-AUTONOMOUS: 430-bp MITE (mPing/miniSNOOPY), GenBank record has NO CDS annotated at all (correctly, since MITEs by definition lack the transposase), mobilized in trans by the autonomous Ping/Mutator-family element per Kikuchi et al 2003.

citation: Moschetti et al. 2008 Mol Genet Genomics 279(5):451-461
why_safe: NON-AUTONOMOUS: GenBank-annotated inverted TIRs (1-17/1249-1265, Bari1-family) are intact, but the internal CDS (135-1131) is explicitly annotated /pseudo (pseudogenized transposase) - TEagle should not call this autonomous.

citation: Turner G, Barbulescu M, Su M, Jensen-Seaman MI, Kidd KK, Lenz J (2001) Curr Biol 11:1531-1535
why_safe: GenBank complete-genome record (9472 bp) annotates both LTRs (1-968, 8504-9472), a gag-pro-pol ORF (1112-6746, with the two -1 frameshifts typical of HML-2) and a putative env ORF (6451-8550, protein AAL18258.1) encoding envelope; full-length, human-specific insertion described by Turner et al. 2001.

citation: Turner G, Barbulescu M, Su M, Jensen-Seaman MI, Kidd KK, Lenz J (2001) Curr Biol 11:1531-1535
why_safe: Complete-genome record (9463 bp), sister locus to K113 from the same study: both LTRs (1-960, 8496-9463) annotated, gag-pro-pol ORF (1104-6740, two -1 frameshifts) and putative env ORF (6442-8541, protein AAL18259.1).

citation: Ono M, Yasunaga T, Miyata T, Ushikubo H (1986) J Virol 60:589-598
why_safe: The original HERV-K10 sequence: GenBank annotates two gag CDS (1112-1963, 1807-3111), a protease-subunit CDS (3639-3917) and both LTRs (1-968, 8212-9179), so gag and protease presence is solid. The downstream pol/env region is annotated in this record as a single long ORF (4172-8257, ~4.1 kb) rather than two separately bounded genes, so the exact pol/env domain boundary is not independently confirmed from this record alone -- use gag/protease at high confidence, env presence at medium confidence pending boundary check against the published ORF map in Ono et al. 1986.

citation: Hanger JJ, Bromham LD, McKee JJ, O'Brien TM, Robinson WF (2000) J Virol 74:4264-4272
why_safe: Complete koala retrovirus (KoRV) genome (8431 bp): gag (961-2526), pol (2641-6024), env (5906-7885) and both LTRs (1-505, 7927-8431) all annotated by the original describing paper. GenBank organism field records the viral taxon (Koala retrovirus); host species (koala) is unambiguous since KoRV is koala-specific and actively endogenizing.

citation: Wang Y, Liu S, Li J, Han M, Wang Z (2008) Virologica Sinica 23:15-24
why_safe: Complete endogenous Jaagsiekte sheep retrovirus (enJSRV) genome (7942 bp) deposited directly under the host organism Ovis aries: gag (583-2433), pro (2325-3194), pol (3440-5742), env (5682-7517), both LTRs (1-435, 7497-7932) annotated.

citation: Tang HB, Ouyang K, Ma L, Bai A, Qin S, Chen F, Lin J, Cao Y, Wu J (2015) Genome Announc 3:e00620-15
why_safe: Complete porcine endogenous retrovirus C (PERV-C) genome (8774 bp): gag (1081-2655), pol (2803-6240, full-length span consistent with intact PR-RT-RNaseH-IN), env (6116-8080), both LTRs (1-639, 8149-8774) annotated. GenBank organism field is the viral taxon (Porcine endogenous retrovirus C); host (domestic pig) is unambiguous for this virus.

citation: Kato S, Matsuo K, Nishimura N, Takahashi N, Takano T (1987) Jpn J Genet 62:127-137
why_safe: Complete baboon endogenous virus (BaEV) strain M7 proviral genome (8507 bp): gag (985-2598), pol (2575-6165), env (6235-7926), both LTRs (1-555, 7953-8507) annotated. The GenBank organism field itself reads 'Baboon endogenous virus strain M7' rather than a host binomial, and the paper's own title describes this as a chimeric genome (gag/pol resembling murine type-C gammaretroviruses, env resembling type-D betaretroviruses); superfamily left blank because the biology is genuinely a natural recombinant, and the exact Papio host species is not stated in the record I could verify.

citation: Herr W (1984) J Virol 49:471-478
why_safe: Complete AKV murine leukemia virus proviral genome (8374 bp) from AKR mice: gag-pol polyprotein ORF (639-5843) with separately annotated gag polyprotein (639-2252) and protease mat_peptide (2238-2612), env polyprotein (5783-7792, gp70+p15E), both LTRs annotated (1-144 and 7825->8374, with terminal reiterations). Host (Mus musculus, AKR strain) is unambiguous for this classical endogenous ecotropic MLV.

citation: Hook LM et al. (2000) J Virol 74:8876-8883
why_safe: Complete endogenous mouse mammary tumor virus Mtv1 proviral genome (9851 bp): gag (1485-3260), pro (3254-4066), pol (4063-6750), env (6536-8602) and sag/superantigen (8550-9497) all separately annotated, plus the frameshift-fusion gag-pro and gag-pro-pol reading frames. LTRs are not explicitly annotated as separate features in this particular GenBank record even though MMTV proviruses are canonically LTR-flanked; domain content (gag/pro/pol/env/sag) is high confidence, LTR presence here is inferred from MMTV biology rather than directly annotated in this record.

citation: Shimode S, Yoshikawa R, Hoshino S, Nakaya Y, Sakaguchi S, Kobayashi T, Miyazawa T (2012) Virus Genes 45:393-397
why_safe: Complete infectious molecular clone (strain UCL) of the feline endogenous retrovirus RD-114 (8409 bp): gag-pol precursor CDS (947-6169), env CDS (6204-7901), both LTRs (1-482, 7928-8409) annotated; one of three clones directly compared in the cited paper.

citation: Shimode S, Yoshikawa R, Hoshino S, Nakaya Y, Sakaguchi S, Kobayashi T, Miyazawa T (2012) Virus Genes 45:393-397
why_safe: Second infectious molecular clone (strain Sc3c) of RD-114 from the same comparison paper: complete genome (8409 bp) with gag-pol precursor CDS (947-6169), env CDS (6204-7901), both LTRs (1-482, 7928-8409) annotated; independent strain from AB705393, useful as a distinct sequence with the same well-characterized architecture.

organism: simian endogenous retrovirus host (Old World monkey; exact species not stated in the record I verified)
citation: van der Kuyl AC, Mang R, Dekker JT, Goudsmit J (1997) J Virol 71:3666-3676
why_safe: Complete simian endogenous type-D retrovirus (SERV) genome (8393 bp), described by the authors as having 'intact genome organization': gag (640-2616), prot (2433-3377, protease/dUTPase, frameshifted), pol (3356-5080, RT, frameshifted), env (6015-7727, GP70/P20E, noted by GenBank to contain a stop codon), both LTRs (1-504, 7915-8393) annotated. Organism binomial for the specific host monkey is not confirmed from the record metadata I retrieved, so only class/superfamily-level and domain-content claims are made with confidence; species-level host identity is left unresolved rather than guessed.

why_safe: Paper reports a 3-primer PCR genotyping assay for a 4.3 kb Jockey-superfamily LINE retrotransposon insertion in the CYP6P5-CYP6P9b intergenic region (chr2, An. funestus).
